chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-Ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), so he said: 'If four months pass and he is kept in suspense (between divorce and return), then either he divorces her or he returns (to conjugal life). I said: 'If he divorces her, does she observe the waiting period of the divorced woman?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: Four months (the duration of the oath)
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The waiting period of the divorced woman
key_terms.وُقِفَ: Kept in suspense (between divorce and return)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a wife if her husband takes an oath of abstention and then divorces her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the procedural outcome of 'Ila', where the husband's silence after four months places the marriage in a state of suspense until he acts. It establishes that if he subsequently divorces her, the wife observes the standard 'iddah' of a revocable divorce, distinguishing it from the waiting period of a widow. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that 'Ila' is not an automatic divorce but a conditional mechanism requiring the husband's final decision to dissolve the bond.
